title: Bengaluru Airport Slashes Departure Fees but Introduces Arrival Charges From September 1
excerpt: AERA's new tariff order cuts domestic departure UDF by 45% to ₹300 while introducing a fee for arriving passengers for the first time at India's third-busiest airport.
body:
• The departure UDF at Kempegowda International Airport will drop to ₹300 for domestic passengers (from ₹550) and ₹997 for international passengers (from ₹1,500) effective September 1.
  • For the first time, arriving passengers at Bengaluru airport will also be charged a User Development Fee, a practice already in place at airports like Delhi and Mumbai.
  • The revised tariff is part of AERA's new five-year control period (FY27-FY31), during which the airport plans a ₹18,635 crore expansion.
  • Bengaluru handled 48.16 million passengers in FY26, making it India's third-busiest airport after Delhi and Mumbai.

Passengers flying through Bengaluru's Kempegowda International Airport will see a significant restructuring of airport charges starting September 1, with the regulator cutting departure fees while extending charges to arriving passengers for the first time.

What Changes for Departing Passengers

The Airports Economic Regulatory Authority of India has ordered a 45% reduction in the User Development Fee for departing domestic passengers, bringing the charge down to ₹300 from the current ₹550. International departure charges will fall to ₹997 from ₹1,500 — a 33% cut.

The reduction brings Bengaluru's domestic departure charges closer to those at Delhi (₹129) and Mumbai (₹175), though it remains higher than both. Among privately operated airports, the revised rate positions Bengaluru as one of the more reasonably priced options.

New Fee for Arriving Passengers

The more consequential change for frequent flyers, particularly NRIs making regular trips to Bengaluru, is the introduction of a UDF on arriving passengers. Until now, Bengaluru airport charged no fee on disembarkation — unlike Delhi and Mumbai, which have levied arrival UDF for years.

The specific rates for arriving passengers have not yet been published in full, but the shift means that round-trip travellers will now face charges in both directions. For diaspora families making annual visits, the cumulative impact across multiple family members could be noticeable.

The ₹18,635 Crore Expansion Behind the Numbers

The tariff restructuring is linked to a massive capital expenditure programme proposed by Bangalore International Airport Ltd for the five-year period from FY27 to FY31. BIAL has submitted a ₹18,635 crore investment plan to AERA, though the regulator's consultant Mecon Ltd has recommended trimming it to ₹13,598 crore — about 27% lower.

BIAL, which is 74% owned by Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings, with the Karnataka government and Airports Authority of India holding 13% each, has argued for smoothing tariffs across the five-year period to avoid sharp increases for passengers while still funding the expansion.

"The annual tariff proposal should be structured in a manner that the eventual UDF and landing rates are smoothened through the 5-year period, while avoiding sharp increases in tariffs."

— Bhaskar Anand Rao, BIAL CFO, in a letter to AERA

What It Means for NRI Travellers

Bengaluru has emerged as a key gateway for the Indian diaspora, particularly those in the technology sector who travel frequently between the US and India. The airport crossed 400 million cumulative passengers in May 2026 and overtook Mumbai as India's second-busiest airport by passenger volume.

The departure fee cut will reduce costs for outbound travellers, but the introduction of arrival charges adds a new line item that did not previously exist. Travellers booking through US-based platforms should note that the fee change takes effect for travel from September 1, regardless of when tickets were purchased.
